settings.assignmentNoteText: After you finish setting up and saving configurations, you must assign them to your Button+ panel devices or to a Group and then assign the group to the devices.
settings.buttonExplanation:
Button Configurations can be applied to one or more Button+ button bars to determine what is displayed.
The button bar is a panel, with 2 mini displays and 2 buttons, that can be used to control On/Off and Dim type devices or run flows.
The Configurations can be applied to physical button bars either in the Homey app's Panel device either individually or via a group or by using Flows
settings.settingsHelpWebView: Open a device web page: Select the Button+ device from Button+ web page, then select Open Web view. The device you open the page from must be on the same network as the Button+.
settings.settingsHelpSimulation: Simulate missing data: When this option is visible, enable it to show sample values when a device, capability, or variable cannot be found. To reveal this option, hold Shift while selecting the Settings tab.
settings.buttonHelpGlobalSettings:
Preview and page controls:
Simulate: Click the On state / Off state button to switch the preview state and check the button text and LEDs. This changes the preview only; it does not operate the device.
Pages: Use the < / > buttons to switch pages, select to add a page, or select to delete one. Each page has its own button settings. On a blank side on a later page, choose Page 0 to reuse its setup or Blank to leave the side empty.
Configurations shown: Choose how many button configurations to compare side by side in the preview (1-4).
Top Extra Settings: Use this toggle and its arrow icon to show or hide editing controls for a more compact preview.
Per-page Extra Settings: Expand this section below a page to configure Click Release Event, Long Press Repeat, Long press delay (ms), Repeat interval (ms), and Broker ID for each side.
settings.displayExplanation:
Display configurations can be applied to one or more large Button+ displays.
Set each item's top-left X and Y positions and its width as percentages of the display dimensions.
You can define multiple items, but make sure they all fit.
settings.displayHelpHowToTitle: How to set up display items
settings.displayHelpConfiguration: Configuration: Choose a Display Configuration at the top. Use the adjacent arrow button to show or edit its name. Each configuration has its own pages and items; use the Copy and Paste to copy one display configuration to another.
settings.displayHelpPages:
Pages: Use the < and > buttons to switch pages. Select to add a page after the current page, or to delete the current page.
Page 0 cannot be deleted and the items defined on it appear on all pages of the Button+.
settings.displayHelpPreviewControls:
Preview controls: Set the status bar to Off, Top, or Bottom with its menu to simulate the Button+ status bar. This does not change the panels status bar as that is configured in the Panel's Advanced settings.
Enable Always show page 0 items to overlay page 0 items on other pages in the preview as they do on the Button+.
settings.displayHelpAddItem: Add an item: Select beside Items. The new item is added to the current page and appears in the preview as a wire frame.
settings.displayHelpConfigureItem: Configure an item: Click on an item in the preview to select it. A selected item has a wire frame around it with tabs to move and size it. A second click opens the properties popup where you can set the Page to choose where it appears, then choose its Device and Capability. Use Label for a title, Unit for a suffix, and Text for a fixed value. For boolean values, set optional On/Off text or SVG. X Position and Y Position set its top-left position; Width sets its size. Use Rounding, Font Size, and Box Type to format it, and Broker ID to choose its MQTT broker.
settings.displayHelpMoveResizeItem: Move or resize: Select the item in the preview. Drag its four-arrow handle located at the top of the item to move it; drag the ↔ handle located on the right side to change its width. You can also enter exact X Position, Y Position, and Width values in the item editor.
settings.displayHelpDeleteItem: Delete an item: Select it in the preview, then select beside Items. You can also use the trash button at the bottom of that item's properties editor. This does not delete the page.
settings.displayHelpCopyPaste: Copy and Paste: Use the buttons below the editor to duplicate a whole Display Configuration or load a copied one.
settings.displayHelpSaveAssign: Save and assign: Select Save All Configurations. Then assign the Display Configuration to your display devices, or include it in a Group and assign that Group to your physical devices.
settings.brokerExplanation:
A Broker is an MQTT server that Button+ and the app connects to for sending and receiving MQTT messages. Add a broker for each MQTT server your devices or topics use. Choose a Default Broker for features that do not select a specific broker.
The app has a built in Broker that can be used if you don't already have an external one setup
settings.brokerHelpDefault: Default Broker: Choose which configured broker the app should use by default when no other Broker ID is selected.
settings.brokerHelpAdd: Add a broker: Select New Broker Item to add a connection, then expand its entry to edit the settings.
settings.brokerHelpFields:
Connection details: Give the broker a unique Broker ID. This ID identifies the broker in configuration selectors and routes messages to the correct broker; each ID must be unique so configurations can distinguish them.
Enter its Address and Port; add a Websocket Port only if your broker provides one. Enter a Username and Password if required by that broker.
settings.brokerHelpEnable: Enable or disable: Turn Enabled on for brokers the app should use. Disabled brokers are not used to send or receive messages.
settings.brokerHelpDelete: Delete a broker: Use the button to remove a user-defined broker. Built-in brokers are protected and cannot be deleted.
settings.brokerHelpSave: Save: Select Save All Configurations to save the broker settings.
settings.diagnosticHelpEnable: Enable full diagnostics Log: Turn this on to capture more diagnostic details. Errors are logged even when it is off.
settings.diagnosticHelpListeners: Get Listeners: Append the current Homey capability listeners to the log text area.
settings.diagnosticHelpClear: Clear Log: Clear the stored diagnostics log.
settings.diagnosticHelpSend: Send Log: Open the support form to add contact details and a description, then send the current log to the developer.
settings.sentLogHelpSelectDevice: Select a panel: Choose the Button+ device whose log you want to view from Button+ web page.
settings.sentLogHelpGet: Get Log: Retrieve the most recent configuration sent to that device. If none has been saved to the device, the log explains that no configuration is available.
settings.sentLogHelpOutput: Log output: The text area shows the retrieved configuration data; select and copy it if you need to inspect or share it.
settings.importExportHelpImport: Import: Paste exported Button+ JSON into the text area, then select Import. Review the imported configurations and select Save All Configurations to apply them.
settings.importExportHelpExport: Export: Select Export to place the current configurations as JSON in the text area, then select and copy the text.
settings.importExportHelpSend: Send Export: Create the current configuration export and open the support form to send it to the developer with a description.
settings.topLabelExplanation: The Top Label is shown along the top of the mini display. It can be used to show the name of the device or flow that is controlled by the button.
settings.toplabelDisplayExplanation: The label is optional text displayed above the value to identify it.
settings.textExplanation: The text to show on the display
settings.label: Label
settings.labelOnExplanation: The labels to show when the button is in the On state. If blank, the button will not latch, so it will switch back to the Off state when released.
settings.labelOffExplanation: The labels to show when the button is in the Off state.
settings.deviceExplanation:
Select the device to control when you press the Button+ button.
Only devices with on/off or dim capabilities are shown.
If you select none, the button won't directly control a device, but you'll still receive the button-press Flow trigger.
settings.deviceDExplanation: Select a Homey device or variable, then choose a capability to display. Select Target Button+ to display values from the Button+ device using this Display Configuration, such as its current page, total pages, brightness, temperature, luminance, free memory, signal strength, date, time, or info.
settings.capabilityExplanation:
Select the capability to show in the button display.
If the capability is read-only or it is a variable, such as an alarm, the button will not toggle the state but the flow triggers will still work.
If the capability is dim, the LED state will be driven by the on/off value and the light can be toggled on / off by double clicking the button. Toggle between + and - by clicking the button.
settings.capabilityDExplanation: Select the capability or variable to show on the display. The list depends on the device selected above.
settings.unitExplanation: The unit is optional text displayed on the same line as the value; it is right-aligned.
settings.xPosExplanation: The X Position is the horizontal position of the left side of the item as a percentage of the display width. Use 0 for the left side and 100 for the right side.
settings.yPosExplanation: The Y Position is the vertical position of the top of the item as a percentage of the display height. Use 0 for the top and 100 for the bottom.
settings.widthExplanation: The Width is the width of the item as a percentage of the display width.
settings.roundingExplanation: The number of decimal places to round the value to. Use 0 for integers.
settings.fontSizeExplanation: The font size to use for the value. The range is from 1 to 4, where 1 is the smallest and 4 is the largest.
settings.dimError: Dim __leftRight__ Change must be between ±1 and ±100. Please correct and try again.
settings.brokerIdExplanation: Select the Broker ID that you want to send and receive messages from.
settings.brokerHomey: This is the app's own broker. It cannot be deleted, but you can disable it if you don't want to use it.
settings.brokerUser: This is a user defined broker. It can be deleted or disabled.
settings.duplicateBrokerIdError: Broker ID '__brokerId__' already exists. Please correct it and try again.
settings.MQTTTopicExplanation: This is an optional custom MQTT topic that will be published when the button is pressed. Leave blank to toggle the Homey device button and trigger a Homey Flow.
settings.dimChangeExplanation:
The amount by which to change the dim level when the button is pressed.
Use a positive or negative number to brighten or darken the device.
For example, +10 increases the dim level by 10% each time the button is pressed, while -10 decreases it by 10%.
If you omit the + or -, the dim level is set to the specified value.
settings.typeExplanation: Select which button event is to be published.
settings.displayTypeExplanation: Select which display element is to be set.
settings.topicExplanation: The MQTT topic to subscribe to.
settings.payloadExplanation: The MQTT payload to match against or send.
settings.MQTTIdExplanation: This is optional for your information only
settings.frontLEDOnColorExplanation: The color of the front LED when the button is in the On state.
settings.wallLEDOnColorExplanation: The color of the wall LED when the button is in the On state.
settings.frontLEDOffColorExplanation: The color of the front LED when the button is in the Off state. Set to black to turn off the LED.
settings.wallLEDOffColorExplanation: The color of the wall LED when the button is in the Off state. Set to black to turn off the LED.
settings.sendLogConfirm: Send the log contents to the developer?
settings.sendSupportMessage: If you click Send, this information will be emailed to the developer.
settings.sendLogPopupMessage: If you click Send, your diagnostics log, email address, and description will be emailed to the developer.
settings.sendExportPopupMessage: If you click Send, your exported configuration, email address, and description will be emailed to the developer.
settings.idExplanation: This is a name you give to the broker to identify it. It must be unique and can't be empty.
settings.addressExplanation: The IP address or URL (normally starting with mqtt://) of the broker.
settings.portExplanation: The port number of the broker. Normally 1883 for MQTT or 8883 for MQTT over SSL, but it might be different if you have a custom broker.
settings.wsPortExplanation: The port number of the broker's websocket. Normally 9001 for MQTT or 9443 for MQTT over SSL.
settings.usernameExplanation: The username to use to connect to the broker. Leave blank if not required.
settings.passwordExplanation: The password to use to connect to the broker. Leave blank if not required.
settings.enabledExplanation: If enabled, the broker can be used to send and receive messages.
settings.brokerButtonPlus: This is the Button Plus public broker for testing. It cannot be deleted, but you can disable it if you don't want to use it.
settings.homeyUsernameExplanation: You can define any username you like to protect the built in MQTT broker or leave it empty to disable user name protection.
settings.homeyPasswordExplanation: You can define any password you like to protect the built in MQTT broker or leave it empty to disable password protection. If you set a password, you must also set a username.
settings.passwordError1: You must set a username if you set a password.
settings.noEnabledBrokerError: You must enable at least one broker.
settings.webviewExplanation:
Select a Homey device from the list, then tap 'Open Web View' to open its simulation page.
The device you're viewing from must be on the same network as the Button+.
settings.enableLLogExplanation:
If enabled, the app will log a lot of diagnostics information.
The app will still log errors even if this is disabled.
settings.simulationExplanation: If enabled, devices, capabilities and variables that cannot be found show simulated data on the panels and in the simulators: 1234.5 for numbers, 'Simulation' for text, On for on/off and the first matching option for lists.
settings.emailExplanation: If you want me to respond to your log, please enter your email address or forum id here so I know how to contact you.
settings.descriptionExplanation: Please enter a brief description of the problem if you are going to send the log.
settings.importExportExplanation:
To import settings, paste the JSON text into the box below and tap the 'Import' button.
To export settings, tap the 'Export' button and then copy the JSON text from the box below.
settings.imported:
Settings have been imported.

Check the configurations and then tap the 'Save All Configurations' button to save them.
settings.exported:
The settings have been copied to the panel.

You can select the text in the panel, copy it to the clipboard and then paste it into a text file or email.
settings.copied:
The settings have been copied.

You can now paste them into another Configuration.
settings.pageExplanation:
Select which page the item should appear on (requires firmware 1.09 or later).
On firmware 2.0.0 or later, page 0 appears on all pages by default.
If there is more than one page, you can switch pages with the left or right Display buttons.
settings.configNameExplanation: Enter a name for the configuration. This is optional but it will help you identify the configuration if you have more than one.
settings.longDelayMsExplanation: Delay from touching the button until the first long press event. Set to 0 for no delay. Values are applied in 10 ms steps.
settings.longRepeatMsExplanation: Delay between repeated long press events. Values are applied in 10 ms steps.
settings.boxTypeExplanation: Select the type of box to display the value in.
settings.customMQTTTopicExplanation: This is an optional custom MQTT topic that will be published when the button is pressed.
settings.buttonPageExplanation:
Button mappings are configured separately for each page. Page 0 is the default/first page; its mappings are not automatically shown on other pages (page support requires firmware 2.0.0 or later).
Use the panel's page controls to switch between pages.
settings.pageHelpIntroMessage: Use this book button to open a guide to the controls and setup examples on each settings page.
settings.buttonHelpSetupType: Select a setup type to show an example
settings.buttonHelpHowToTitle: How to set up a button
settings.buttonHelpClickTitle: Title: Click the yellow title area to edit it. Enter any short text you want, such as a room or device name.
settings.buttonHelpClickValue: Value: Click the white value area to choose the capability or variable shown on the display. This display source can be different from the capabilities controlled by button events.
settings.buttonHelpLED: LEDs: In STD, click the front or wall LED in the preview to open its color settings, then choose the On and Off colors. In ADV, click the LED area to open the LED settings; choose a source device and capability. Boolean values select the On/Off colors, while numeric values blend between them. For a numeric source, an optional on/off capability can force the LEDs off when the device is off. The LED source is independent of the display and button-action sources.
settings.buttonHelpClearButton: Clear this button side on the current page. The other side and other pages are not affected.
settings.buttonHelpPageFallback: On a blank button on page 1 or higher, choose Page 0 to reuse that side's page-0 setup, or Blank to leave it empty. This control only appears when the side is blank in STD mode; page-specific settings are never overwritten.
settings.buttonHelpToggleModeStd: Simple setup for one device, its displayed value, and LED colors.
settings.buttonHelpToggleModeAdv: Configure separate actions for click, double-click, and long-press, plus independent display and LED sources.
settings.buttonHelpAdvancedButton: In ADV mode, click the green BUTTON pill to open Advanced mappings for each event type (Click, Double Click and Long Press). Choose the device and capability for each event, and set separate display and LED sources.
settings.buttonHelpWizard: Opens the setup wizard. Choose a device type and device to fill in suggested title, display, LED, and event settings; review and adjust them afterward.
settings.buttonHelpSaveAssign: Save and assign: Select Save All Configurations. Then assign each Button Configuration to its Button+ panel devices, or add it to a Group and assign that Group to the devices.
settings.buttonHelpSetupFlowOnly:
1. Choose a mode:
    STD for a simple press.
    ADV for separate click, double-click, and long-press Flow triggers.
  2. Configure the matching option:
    STD Click the value area and set Device to None.
    ADV Click the green BUTTON, choose an event, set Target Device to None, and set Action / Capability to Flow Trigger Only.

Choose this when a Homey Flow should decide what the press does.
settings.buttonHelpSetupOnOff:
1. Select STD.
  2. Click the value area. In the main button fields set Device to the light, switch, or socket, and Capability to onoff. Edit the On/Off text or SVG here if wanted.
  3. Click the title area to set Top Label.
  4. Click the LED area and choose Front/Wall LED On/Off colors.

A click toggles the device and selects its On or Off text/SVG. Choose this for straightforward power control.
settings.buttonHelpSetupDimmable:
1. Select ADV.
  2. Click the value area. Set Device to the light and Capability to dim to show its level.
  3. Click the green BUTTON pill. In Click, set Target Device to the light and Action / Capability to onoff if click should toggle power.
  4. In Long/repeat, set Target Device to the light, Action / Capability to dim, and Value Step to +10 or -10.
  5. Click the LED area. Set LED Source Device to the light and LED Source Capability to dim. Choose Front/Wall On and Off colors; they blend from Off to On as brightness rises from 0% to 100%. Optionally set LED on/off capability to onoff so the LEDs turn off with the light.

Choose this for one button that controls both power and brightness.
settings.buttonHelpSetupThermostat:
1. Select ADV.
  2. Click the value area. Set Device to the thermostat and Capability to target_temperature.
  3. Click the green BUTTON pill. For Click and Long/repeat, set Target Device to the thermostat and Action / Capability to target_temperature.
  4. Set each event's Value Step, for example +1 for Click and +2 for Long/repeat. Use a negative step for the opposite direction.
  5. For LED feedback, click the LED area and set LED Source Device to the thermostat and LED Source Capability to target_temperature. The numeric setpoint blends the chosen Front/Wall Off and On colors across its capability range.

Choose this when the button should display and adjust the setpoint.
settings.buttonHelpSetupThermostatDisplay:
1. Select ADV.
  2. Click the value area. Set Device to the thermostat and Capability to measure_temperature.
  3. Click the green BUTTON pill. For Click and Long/repeat, set Target Device to the thermostat and Action / Capability to target_temperature.
  4. Set each event's Value Step, such as +0.5 or +1. The first event previews the setpoint and direction; later events, while the preview is displayed, adjust it.
  5. For LED feedback, click the LED area and set LED Source Device to the thermostat and LED Source Capability to measure_temperature. Its numeric value blends the chosen Front/Wall Off and On colors across its capability range.

Choose this to show current temperature at rest while controlling the separate setpoint.
settings.buttonHelpSetupWindowCoverings:
1. Select ADV.
  2. Click the value area. Set Device to the blind/curtain and Capability to windowcoverings_set or windowcoverings_state, depending on what you want displayed.
  3. Click the green BUTTON pill. For Click or Long/repeat, set Target Device to the blind/curtain and Action / Capability to windowcoverings_set.
  4. Set Value Step as a percentage, such as +10 for a small move or +100 for a full move.
  5. For position-based LED feedback, click the LED area and select the numeric position capability as LED Source Capability. Choose Front/Wall On and Off colors; they blend between those colors as the position changes from 0% to 100%.

Choose this to move blinds or curtains and show their position.
settings.buttonHelpSetupColour:
1. Select ADV.
  2. Click the green BUTTON pill. For the event that changes hue, set Target Device to the color light, Action / Capability to light_hue, and Value Step to a small amount such as +0.1.
  3. Click the LED area. Set LED Source Device to the light and LED Source Capability to light_hue. The LEDs use the light's current hue, and the fixed On/Off color controls are hidden for this source. Optionally set LED on/off capability to onoff; when the light is off, the LEDs show black.

Choose this to adjust a color light and have its LEDs follow the light's color.
settings.buttonHelpSetupFan:
1. Select ADV.
  2. Click the value area. Set Device to the fan and Capability to the speed or mode you want displayed.
  3. Click the green BUTTON pill. For power, set Click Target Device to the fan and Action / Capability to onoff.
  4. For speed, set Long/repeat Target Device to the fan and Action / Capability to dim. For fan modes, choose the writable mode capability instead.
  5. For speed-based LED feedback, set the fan as LED Source Device, choose dim as LED Source Capability, and choose Front/Wall On and Off colors. They blend as speed changes; optionally set the LED on/off capability to onoff.

Choose this to control fan power and, where supported, speed or mode.
settings.buttonHelpSetupLock:
1. Select ADV.
  2. Click the value area. Set Device to the lock and Capability to locked or locked_status for the displayed state.
  3. Click the green BUTTON pill. Set Click Target Device to the lock and Action / Capability to its writable locked capability.
  4. Set Relock after (seconds) in the Click section if it should lock automatically after unlocking.
  5. Click the LED area to set lock-state colors or a source.

Choose this when the lock provides one writable toggle capability.
settings.buttonHelpSetupLockButtons:
1. Select ADV.
  2. Click the value area. Set Device to the lock and Capability to locked_status or another status capability.
  3. Click the green BUTTON pill. Set Click Target Device to the lock and Action / Capability to unlock.
  4. Assign lock or deadbolt to a separate Double-click or Long/repeat event using that event's Target Device and Action / Capability.
  5. Set Relock after (seconds) on the unlock event if needed.

Choose this when the lock exposes separate unlock, lock, or deadbolt commands.
settings.buttonHelpSetupReadOnly:
1. Select STD.
  2. Click the value area. Set Device to the sensor and Capability to the value or status to display.
  3. Click the title area to set Top Label, then click the LED area to set colors.
  4. To make button presses run a Flow, leave Device as None; or switch to ADV and set the event's Action / Capability to Flow Trigger Only.

Choose this to display live, read-only data without trying to write to the sensor.
settings.buttonHelpSetupCustomMQTT:
1. Select STD.
  2. In the main button fields set Device to Custom MQTT. Capability can remain empty.
  3. Open this side's Custom MQTT Topics section, add the topic and payload, and choose the Broker ID.
  4. Click the LED area to set optional Front/Wall colors.

Choose this when a press should publish MQTT rather than write to a Homey capability.
settings.sentLogPageHelp: This page shows the most recent configuration uploaded to a Button+ panel. Select a panel to retrieve its sent configuration log.
settings.pageError: The new page number must be greater than 0 and less than the number of pages.
settings.displaySimStatusBarHint: This status bar setting affects only the emulator's appearance on this screen. The actual status bar for each Button+ is configured in that device's Advanced Settings.
settings.displaySimShowDefaultItemsHint: Page 0 items appear on all pages. You can turn this off in the preview but be careful of adding items that overlap page 0 items.
settings.displaySimTotalPagesHint: Number of additional pages excluding the default page
settings.displaySimEmptyMessage: Tap on the + button in the Items footer to add an item
settings.unsavedSettingsDetectedMessage: Unsaved settings were detected. Would you like to restore them?
settings.dimValueExplanation: Specifies how much the dim button changes the brightness level on each repeat of the long press
settings.numericValueStepExplanation: A value without a sign sets the target directly. Prefix + or - to change the current value by that amount. Brightness and blind values are percentages.
settings.advancedMappingTargetHelp: Choose the Homey device and writable capability for this event. Flow Trigger Only runs the Flow without changing a device. Toggle direction switches this button between + and - without writing a value. Missing devices/capabilities are marked (Missing); simulation shows sample values only and does not write to devices.
settings.advancedMappingPreviewHelp: If the event target differs from the displayed capability, the first event shows the target's current value and direction for 3 seconds without changing it. Later events change the value while the preview is visible. After the display returns to its SVG, the next event previews again. Matching display and event capabilities change immediately. A click may wait briefly for double-click detection; long press repeats.
settings.unableToAddPage: Unable to add a new page.
settings.selectDeviceFromListError: Please select a device from the list
settings.clickZonesHelpTooltip:
Click title to edit the top label.
Click value text to edit the state value.
Click icon area to edit SVG.
Click Button to open advanced mappings.
settings.buttonWizardHint: Pick a device type and device. The button will be switched to advanced mode and its title, value, LEDs and click, double-click and long-press actions will be set up for that device.
settings.relockSecondsExplanation: When this action unlocks the lock, it is locked again after this many seconds. Set to 0 to disable.
settings.advancedModeTooltip:
Enable this per side when you need more than simple on/off behaviour.
Map click, double-click and long/repeat to different devices or capabilities, including numeric step actions.
Choose separate sources for display content and LED state so visuals can follow a different capability than the action target.
settings.configurationHasNoPage: This configuration has no page here
settings.groupExplanation: A Panel Group represents a complete physical Button+ panel (Display module + Button connector modules). Assign a Display Configuration and up to 8 Button Configurations (Connectors 0 to 7) to a Group, preview the panel in the simulator, and assign the Group to your physical devices.
settings.groupHelpHowToTitle: How to set up a Panel Group
settings.groupHelpManage: Choose a group: Select a group from Select Group. Use its ↴ button to show or edit Group Name.
settings.groupHelpActions: Manage groups: Use to create a group, to duplicate it, or to delete it.
settings.groupHelpPreview: Preview / Configure: Select Preview to hide the group setup controls and Save button for a cleaner simulator view. Select Configure to show the controls again.
settings.groupHelpPages: Pages: The page title shows the current page and total page count. Use the < and > buttons beside it to move between pages; the simulator updates the display and button bars together.
settings.groupHelpDisplayModule: Display Module: This appears first in the simulator. If none is assigned, select Add Display Module. Select its numbered circle 1 to choose a Display Configuration; select to open that configuration, or to remove it from this group without deleting the configuration.
settings.groupHelpButtonBars:
Button Bar Modules: Each bar appears below the Display Module.
Select its numbered circle 1 to assign a Button Configuration.
Select to open that configuration in the button editor;
use ↑ / ↓ to change connector order, or to remove the bar from this group without deleting its configuration. Click either simulated button to toggle its preview state.
settings.groupHelpAddButtonBars: Add Button Bar Modules: Select Add Button Bar Module at the bottom of the simulator. A group can contain up to 8 button bars (Connectors 0-7). if the Button+ doesn't have enough connectors the excess bars will just not be used.
settings.groupHelpSaveAssign: Save and assign: Select Save All Configurations to save the group. Then assign the Group to your physical Button+ devices in their device settings.

repair.intro:
Use this option when you add or remove buttons or when the IP address has changed.

If the IP address has changed then correct it below.
Tap on repair to update the connector map and save the device settings.
repair.title: Repair device settings

hello2: Open the Button+ Homey app settings to setup configurations
hello3: Then use the Button+ Homey device to assign configurations to the physical buttons and displays
